title: The Mersey Otters

evidence.name: Rainbow Sheen
evidence.text: An oily rainbow film at the brook's outfall, and a smell like a freshly pressed suit. That is solvent, not weedkiller.

evidence.name: Delivery Docket
evidence.text: From the dockside porter: four drums of cleaning solvent signed for by 'D.P.', for a yard on the Wirral. Last delivery a fortnight ago.

evidence.name: Tuesday at Dusk
evidence.text: The fish only turn up belly-up on Wednesdays. Something goes in on Tuesday evening, on the ebb, when the tide carries it out of sight.

evidence.name: Rooke's Complaint
evidence.text: A stiff letter to the council: otters have rooted up Director Rooke's bowling green and he wants 'something done'. Shouty, but about turf, not tins.

evidence.name: Green Waders
evidence.text: Mavis Crabtree's waders are stained green-black to the knee. Pondweed and brook mud. She has been sampling the water for the angling club since March.

evidence.name: Chester Season Ticket
evidence.text: Director Rooke holds a season ticket for Chester Racecourse, and Tuesdays are race days. He is rarely home before ten.

evidence.name: Van Tracks
evidence.text: By the culvert: tyre marks of a small van, and a flattened carrier bag printed POLLITT'S LAUNDERETTE AND DRY CLEANING. Not subtle.

suspects.name: Director Rooke
suspects.wrong: Me? I fence things. I do not tip things. I do not even like the word 'tip'. I wrote to the council about my bowling green, and that is the full extent of my war on otters. I shall be writing to your mother.

suspects.name: Mavis Crabtree
suspects.wrong: Me?! Forty years I've fished that brook! I've put more fish back than you've had hot dinners! Right, that's it, I'm taking this to the committee. There will be minutes.

suspects.name: Dennis Pollitt
suspects.right: Alright, alright. It's the dry-cleaning solvent. The disposal firm wants ninety quid a drum and I thought, it's a brook, it's big, it'll mind itself. I never gave the otters a thought. I'll pay for the clean-up. And, er, the fish.

steps.text: Speak to Warden Bell on the Wirral Way.
Look at the brook's outfall on the Wirral Way for anything unusual.
Ask Mavis Crabtree of the angling club, on the Wirral Way.
Ask the dockside porter in Liverpool what the sheen could be.
Question Director Rooke at the Port Building in Liverpool.
Call on Dennis Pollitt in Wirral.
Check the culvert by the Wirral Way for tracks.
Report back to Warden Bell on the Wirral Way.

accuse_hint: Warden Bell is waiting on the Wirral Way.
closed: The brook runs clear again, and an otter has been seen on the Wirral Way, looking smug.
